reason: The direct question gets a good answer. "No, don't make up the miles" is clear and right, and the reassurance about stringing together steady weeks is sound. The doctor flag for lingering tiredness, the rest days and the heart-rate caps on easy days all help, and each day can be run as written. But the tiredness only gets a sleep note and a referral. The training load doesn't change: volume rises about 15% on what she actually ran, and there's still a quality day and a 12 mi long run. Two weeks of falling mileage with "drained" should mean a truly easier week, not a step back up toward the plan. The draft also brings in things the card doesn't mention, a "deadline" and "the heat," so it reads partly generic or invented, and the "2 mi cut from Sunday" can't be checked against the card. The answer to her question is sound, but the plan's progression ignores how run down she is, which keeps the rating low.

── MARISOL'S WEEK ──
Marisol is training for a second marathon, the Wexley Lakes Marathon, aiming to break 3:45 after a 4:02 debut. Marisol runs five days a week, with a session on Wednesday, the long run on Sunday and Monday and Friday off, and ran about 30 miles a week before this build.
Recent weeks: 32, 35, 32, 24 mi
This week: 27 mi over 4 runs. Planned 36 mi, ran 27 mi. Missed 1 of 5 planned runs.
Body: "Tired all the time. Knee is fine."
Feeling: "Drained."
Asks: "I missed Thursday and cut the long run short. Should I make up the miles next week?"

── THE DRAFT ──
Tells Marisol: Skip the make-up miles. …
Answers: (1) No, don't make up the miles. You've lost the missed Thursday and the 2 mi cut from Sunday, and that's fine. (2) Your fitness for Nov 1 will come from stringing together steady weeks over the next two months, not from any single run. Next week is about 31 mi with a 12 mi long run.
Safety flag: Know the heat warning signs
Safety flag: See a doctor if the tiredness lingers
Next week:
Mon: rest. Sleep is the best training you can do while the deadline and the heat last.
Tue: easy, 5 mi, heart rate under 145 at whatever pace that takes, before sunrise or on…
Wed: quality, 6 mi: 1.5 mi easy, 3 x 1 mi at marathon effort (about 8:35/mi in cool air…
Thu: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 145, then 15 min hip and glute routine. Skip the run…
Fri: rest. Keeps your legs fresh for the weekend.
Sat: easy, 4 mi, heart rate under 145, early morning, flat route. Loosens the legs…
Sun: long, 12 mi, heart rate under 150, start at first light, carry water and drink…
